headline: GOLD ENTERS CRITICAL CPI WEEK AT $4,121 — FIRST NEGATIVE MONTHLY JUNE READ FORECAST; WARSH TESTIMONY FOLLOWS MONDAY
snippet: Gold enters the most important week of H2 2026 trading at approximately $4,121 per ounce, pinned in a tight $4,060–$4,157 consolidation range ahead of the June CPI print due Monday July 14 at 8:30 a.m. ET — followed 90 minutes later by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's congressional testimony. The consensus CPI estimate calls for the first negative monthly headline reading in recent memory: -0.1% month-over-month, driven by crude oil's slide toward $68/barrel removing the energy-component inflation that kept the hawkish FOMC majority intact through Q2. The prior month's reading was +0.5% MoM at 4.2% year-over-year; a -0.1% June print would represent the sharpest one-month deceleration in the current tightening cycle. If the print lands at or below consensus, September rate-hike probability — currently at approximately 53% on CME FedWatch — collapses below 30%, breaking the dollar's technical support and potentially clearing the primary mechanical headwind that has kept gold below $4,300 since January's correction from $5,500. A soft CPI plus a balanced or cautious Warsh statement is the 'squeeze setup': with COMEX managed-money gold net longs already retreating 13% from January peaks to approximately 194,000 contracts, the positioning is lean enough for a sharp recovery rally targeting the August 2025 volume gap between $4,400 and $4,500. The bear case: a 4.2%+ year-over-year print consistent with May's reading confirms Warsh's hawkish posture and extends gold's consolidation below $4,150 into late July. The Cleveland Fed's inflation nowcast — projecting negative monthly CPI reads for both June and July, driven by WTI crude price retreat — is the best leading indicator of which scenario materialises Monday morning.

headline: ISS AND PROXY ADVISORS BACK $5.1B EQUINOX/ORLA GOLD MERGER — VOTE JULY 22; PROXY DEADLINE MONDAY (TSX:EQX)
snippet: Both ISS (Institutional Shareholder Services) and independent proxy advisory firms published recommendations on July 10 that Equinox Gold shareholders vote FOR the share issuance resolution authorising up to 421.8 million new Equinox Gold shares to complete the all-share acquisition of Orla Mining Ltd., valued at US$5.1 billion (1.00 Equinox Gold share plus US$0.0001 cash per Orla share). The July 22 special shareholder meeting is now 10 days away; the proxy voting deadline is 9 a.m. Vancouver time Monday July 20. ISS framed the deal as making 'strategic sense' by diversifying Equinox's asset base and enhancing long-term production potential: the combined entity would target approximately 1.1 million gold-equivalent ounces per year across assets in Canada, Mexico, Brazil, and the United States — creating North America's next senior gold producer. The board transition underscores the deal's significance: Equinox chairman Ross Beaty, one of Canadian mining's most respected capital allocators with more than 35 years of track record, steps aside at close in favour of Charles Jeannes, former CEO of Goldcorp and an architect of the 2019 Newmont/Goldcorp merger. Existing Equinox and former Orla shareholders would own approximately 67% and 33% of the combined company respectively. For investors tracking North American gold sector M&A, the Equinox/Orla combination is the most significant mid-tier consolidation underway in 2026: the combined entity's production profile and balance sheet will become the new benchmark for North American producer comps relative to senior peers Agnico Eagle and Kinross. If the vote passes July 22, a rapid re-rating of the combined entity versus its nearest senior-producer peers is the primary near-term equity catalyst.

headline: COT JULY 11: GOLD NET LONG RETREATS 13% FROM PEAK — 194,000 CONTRACTS; LEAN POSITIONING SETS UP SHARP CPI SQUEEZE
snippet: The CFTC's Commitments of Traders report released Friday July 11 shows COMEX gold managed-money net longs at approximately 194,246 contracts (233,713 longs versus 39,467 shorts) as of the Tuesday July 7 positioning snapshot. The net long has retreated roughly 13% from January's speculative peak — a meaningful reduction in the 'crowded long' risk that constrained gold's rally capacity during Q2, when profit-taking from over-leveraged speculative positions repeatedly overwhelmed positive fundamental catalysts. Silver positioning is notably different and arguably more bullish: silver managed-money net longs have returned to near-neutral territory, with the long/short ratio compressed to approximately 3.4:1 — a positioning structure historically consistent with significant short-covering acceleration once a macro catalyst arrives. USD net positioning adds a currency overlay: non-commercial dollar shorts are near their largest since early 2025, meaning a soft June CPI print that weakens the dollar is double-leverage for gold — the metal rises in USD terms as the dollar falls and real yield expectations drop simultaneously. The practical read for investors: the January-to-July de-leveraging in gold speculative positioning has done the technical work required to set up the next bull market leg. Crowded longs punish bull markets by converting any buyer into a potential seller; a 194,000-contract net long at $4,100 gold — with PBOC structural buying intact at 20 consecutive months and central bank demand globally elevated — is a significantly cleaner starting point than the January peak at $5,500 gold. Monday's CPI is not merely incremental data; it is the ignition test for a positioning-cleared trade.

headline: GOLDMAN HOLDS $5,400 GOLD AS BOFA CUTS TO $4,360 — WIDEST INSTITUTIONAL FORECAST GAP IN MODERN HISTORY
snippet: The divergence between Goldman Sachs and Bank of America on gold is now the widest in recent memory — a $1,040 per ounce spread between two major institutions for the same twelve-month period. Goldman Sachs is maintaining its year-end 2026 gold price target of US$5,400 per ounce, citing what its commodity team calls an 'unprecedented structural demand floor' from central bank purchases running at 20+ consecutive months globally, with the PBOC adding 14.93 tonnes in June alone — the largest single-month purchase since October 2023. Goldman's bull case requires: the Fed to pause or begin cutting rates by Q4 2026, the dollar to weaken as U.S. fiscal risks reassert at sub-$4,100 gold, and the central-bank buying bloc to continue absorbing Western institutional outflows. Bank of America, by contrast, cut its 2026 average gold price forecast to US$4,360 per ounce on July 8 — assigning 50%+ probability to at least one Fed hike before year-end under Warsh, whose 9-to-8 FOMC vote split signals a hawkish majority that BofA believes gold cannot structurally overcome until policy pivots. The $5,400 vs. $4,360 gap represents the highest institutional forecast dispersion in modern history for a single-year outlook on the same asset. For retail investors, the disagreement is a signal: when major institutions are this divided on an asset with PBOC structural buying at $4,100 gold, the resolution historically rewards those positioned before consensus reforms. Goldman's $5,400 target from current prices implies approximately 31% upside. At all-in sustaining costs the major miners are reporting ($1,725/oz average for GDX top-25), a $5,400 gold price would produce unit profits above $3,600/oz — new record territory that would re-rate the sector from current historic NAV discounts.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE HITS 10-WEEK LOW AT 155,000 CNY/T — CATL JIANXIAWO MINE RESTART THREATENS 3% GLOBAL SUPPLY RETURN
snippet: Lithium carbonate futures in China fell to approximately 155,000 yuan per tonne as of July 10 — a 10-week low representing an approximate 10% decline over two trading sessions — after the Jiangxi Provincial Department of Natural Resources issued a 'Project Land Use Pre-Approval and Site Selection Opinion' for CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine in Yichun, valid from June 17, 2026 through June 17, 2029. The approval clears a significant regulatory hurdle for a mine that was suspended in August 2025 when its original permit expired. Jianxiawo is capable of producing approximately 46,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate annually — roughly 3% of current global lithium supply — meaning its full resumption would meaningfully add to a market that Citi analysts characterise as remaining 'relatively tight' with significant new battery capacity coming online in Q3 2026. Critical nuance: the land pre-review is not the same as resuming operations. The mine still requires a renewed mining permit, updated environmental impact reviews, and formal approval for a tailings storage facility — a regulatory sequence that analysts estimate could take 12–24 months. Near-term price pressure reflects market fear of supply return rather than actual incremental tonnes. The longer-term structural picture remains constructive: EV sales continue growing, new battery capacity is coming online in Q3–Q4 2026, and even if Jianxiawo fully restarts by early 2027, the added supply enters a market with durable secular demand growth. For investors holding Western lithium explorer positions — Sigma Lithium, Patriot Battery Metals, Standard Lithium — the Jianxiawo restart speculation creates near-term technical headwinds but does not alter the multi-year supply deficit thesis that underpins structurally elevated lithium prices.

headline: URANIUM $85.75/LB STEADY AS US DOMESTIC OUTPUT HITS MULTI-YEAR HIGH — LONG-TERM CONTRACTS TIGHTER THAN SPOT PRICE SUGGESTS
snippet: U.S. domestic uranium production has increased substantially in 2026 while COMEX spot prices have held steady in the $85–$86/lb range — a combination that reflects a bifurcated market where spot is quiescent and long-term contract prices are climbing, reported the American Nuclear Society's Nuclear Newswire on July 7. Uranium spot settled at $85.75/lb on July 10, flat month-over-month but up 19.5% year-over-year, trading in a narrow $83–$87 range since April after the speculative-driven surge to $101/lb in January reversed. The mechanism: utilities satisfied near-term delivery needs from long-term contracts signed in 2024–2025 when Russian supply disruption created urgency, leaving spot with limited buy-side pressure even as structural demand additions accumulate. Those structural additions are substantive: Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft have all signed agreements to procure new nuclear generating capacity for AI data centre operations, joining the broader wave of government nuclear programmes (UK, Poland, Japan, South Korea) committing to new reactor builds in 2025–2026. Domestic U.S. production growth has important policy implications: if Section 232 restrictions on foreign uranium imports are extended to cover additional product categories in H2 2026, domestic producers including Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU), Ur-Energy (NYSE: URG), and Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE: UEC) benefit from reduced import competition at the margin. For junior uranium explorers on the TSXV and ASX, the combination of $85/lb spot, rising long-term contract valuations, and AI-driven incremental demand represents the most favourable structural backdrop for new project financing since the pre-Fukushima market peak in 2007.

headline: GOLDGROUP AND GOLD RESOURCE $372M MEXICO GOLD MERGER CLOSING THIS WEEK JULY 17 — CERRO PRIETO AND DON DAVID MINES COMBINING
snippet: The US$372 million business combination between Goldgroup Mining Inc. and Gold Resource Corporation, approved by shareholders of both companies on July 2, 2026, is scheduled to close on or about Friday July 17 — creating a multi-mine Mexico-and-Michigan-focused precious metals producer with four producing or advanced assets. The combined portfolio spans Goldgroup's Cerro Prieto mine and San Francisco project in Sonora, Mexico; Gold Resource Corporation's Don David gold-silver-copper-zinc mine in Oaxaca, Mexico; and the Back Forty zinc-gold-silver-copper project in Michigan, which holds a significant polymetallic resource base. At current spot prices — gold at $4,121, silver at approximately $59/oz — the Mexico-focused operating platform benefits directly from peso weakness that has compressed operating costs relative to USD revenues throughout 2026, a structural advantage that Mexico-focused producers have exploited during the precious metals correction as peso-denominated costs declined while USD revenues held at elevated levels. The deal is structured as an all-share combination, meaning both shareholder bases participate in any re-rating of the combined entity. For investors monitoring Mexico-focused mining consolidation, the Goldgroup/Gold Resource transaction reflects a pattern emerging across the mid-tier sector: operators with positive cash flow at $4,000+ gold are choosing to combine rather than dilute equity at depressed share prices, positioning the merged entities for accelerated re-rating when the gold bull market's next leg materialises. The July 17 close is this Friday.

headline: SKY GOLD HITS NEW PROPERTY RECORD 48.56 g/t Au AT EVENING STAR NEVADA — 300M WALKER LANE GOLD-COPPER TREND OUTLINED (TSXV:SKYG)
snippet: Sky Gold Corp. (TSXV: SKYG) reported July 9 that surface sampling at the Evening Star Project on Nevada's Walker Lane Gold Trend returned a grab sample of 48.56 g/t gold — the highest gold value recorded on the property to date — directly east of the Good Hope target area, extending the known mineralised footprint. Soil sampling at the Golden Bomber target outlined a 300-metre northwest-trending gold-copper-lead-silver anomaly, with additional surface sampling returning 14.98 g/t Au and 9.23 g/t Au at multiple points along strike. Two inaugural diamond drill holes (ES-26-01 and ES-26-02) intersected anomalous quartz-vein zones 17.8 metres and 13.8 metres wide respectively — below ore-grade but establishing the structural framework and geometry for the mineralised system. The company appropriately cautions that grab samples are selective and non-representative of bulk mineralisation, framing the 48.56 g/t Au reading as a targeting tool rather than a resource indicator. The Walker Lane context matters: the corridor hosting Coeur Mining's Rochester Mine, i-80 Gold's operations, and several of Nevada's highest-grade vein deposits has a well-established geological template where high-grade surface samples from structurally controlled quartz veins are legitimate precursors to bulk-mineable open-pit or underground gold systems. Sky Gold plans Phase 2 drilling targeting the depth extension of the quartz-vein zones identified in Phase 1, using the 300-metre surface trend as the drill-fence geometry. At sub-$10M market cap levels typical for early-stage Walker Lane explorers, a highest-ever-on-property surface grade reading plus a drill-ready 300-metre surface trend is the combination that attracts Phase 2 financing conversations.

headline: ENERGY FUELS STARTS HEAVY REE CIRCUIT MODS AT WHITE MESA — COMMERCIAL DYSPROSIUM, TERBIUM TARGET Q4 2026 (NYSE:UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU, TSX: EFR) is commencing modifications to the Phase 1 rare earth separation circuits at its White Mesa Mill in Utah during July 2026 — the start of engineering work to enable commercial-scale production of dysprosium (Dy), terbium (Tb), samarium (Sm), europium (Eu), and gadolinium (Gd) oxides from existing feed sources. Commercial production of these heavy REEs is targeted for Q4 2026, with annual installed capacity planned at 48 metric tonnes of Dy oxide and 14 metric tonnes of Tb oxide. The strategic significance is substantial: Energy Fuels' White Mesa Mill is currently the only facility in the Western Hemisphere capable of producing separated heavy rare earth element oxides outside Chinese-controlled supply chains, and the modifications announced for July bring Dy and Tb commercial production timelines to the earliest available in the non-Chinese heavy REE supply chain. At July 2026 spot prices — dysprosium up 25.4% in the month alone, terbium at approximately $4,500/kg — the revenue value of full-capacity Dy and Tb production from White Mesa would represent meaningful incremental value relative to Energy Fuels' uranium-only revenue base. The defence application context is urgent: dysprosium is essential for the permanent magnets in missile guidance systems, military vehicle motors, and radar equipment — the exact applications for which European and U.S. defence contractors reported acute supply shortages in Q2 2026 after China's export licensing regime restricted access. A U.S. domestic Dy/Tb supply source entering commercial production in Q4 2026 directly addresses the most acute vulnerability in the Western defence supply chain for strategic materials.

headline: OROSUR MINING DRILLS BENEATH 79.6 g/t Au HIT AT PEPAS WEST COLOMBIA — 200M STRIKE EXTENSION TARGETED (TSXV:OMI)
snippet: Orosur Mining Inc. (TSXV: OMI, AIM: OMI) has commenced diamond drilling beneath a 79.6 g/t gold surface rock sample identified along strike from the Pepas West discovery at the Anzá Project in Colombia's Mid-Cauca gold belt, approximately 30 kilometres west of Medellín. The 79.6 g/t Au grab sample is the company's strongest surface gold reading at Anzá and is located approximately 200 metres along strike from Pepas West's main zone — where drilling in 2025–2026 confirmed vein-hosted gold mineralisation at grades up to 3.46 g/t Au across multi-metre intercepts in five step-out holes (PEP095–PEP099). The current drilling program targets the depth extension of the high-grade surface expression, with the geological interpretation that the 79.6 g/t outcrop represents surfacing of the same mineralised vein system controlling Pepas West at depth. If confirmed at depth with comparable grades, Orosur would have extended Pepas West's mineralised footprint by approximately 200 metres — nearly doubling the defined system's strike length at Anzá. The Mid-Cauca gold belt context is instructive: the corridor hosts AngloGold Ashanti's massive Quebradona copper-gold project and has produced several significant discoveries since 2018, establishing the district's endowment credentials. Orosur's Anzá exploration is small-scale and early-stage, but in vein-hosted epigenetic gold systems like Pepas West, strong surface-to-depth grade correlation in initial holes is the key technical prerequisite for a maiden resource definition — and the current drilling beneath a 79.6 g/t surface sample is precisely the test that matters most at this stage.

headline: GOLD MINING STOCKS WINNERS AND LOSERS AT THE H2 2026 START — LEVERAGED RECOVERY BETS IF CPI BREAKS HAWKISH CONSENSUS
snippet: Analysis published on Investing.com in July 2026 examines which precious metals equities are best positioned to benefit from a gold and silver recovery in H2 2026, framing the current correction from January's $5,500 peak as a setup rather than a secular reversal. The key structural points: roughly half of annual silver demand is now industrial (solar panels, EVs, electronics), providing a demand floor that operates independently of investment sentiment, while physical gold's central bank bid — with nearly 90% of surveyed central banks planning to add gold reserves in the next 12 months — creates a price support mechanism that did not exist in prior bear markets. The mining equity investment case is fundamentally earnings-driven: gold mining majors reporting Q2 2026 results beginning in late July will show implied unit profits of approximately $2,787 per ounce — the second-best quarter in sector history — against a market pricing the sector at historic NAV discounts built during a 15-year gold bear market. A rate-sensitive correction that produced 25–30% declines in GDX and GDXJ from January highs has created conditions where each dollar of gold price recovery translates to $3–4 of EBITDA improvement per mined ounce, maximising earnings leverage at exactly the moment when the primary macro catalyst (June CPI, July 14) is approaching. For retail investors in junior mining, the H2 2026 setup is a function of two variables converging within the next 30 days: whether gold's macro headwinds ease post-CPI, and whether the junior-to-senior valuation gap — at historic extremes in July 2026 — normalises as major producers trade toward fundamental NAV and re-rate their smaller peers with them.
